description: LinkedIn's loop pivoted heavily in 2025 — Staff candidates now sit a packed two-round phone screen (coding + project retro) before a five-round onsite that includes an AI-Coding session in CoderPad's assistant pane. Behavioural depth is the dominant downlevel axis; the same coding bar that passes at Senior frequently caps a Staff loop with a downlevel offer.
note: Question block only. The site's answer body is not included here; the untouched page is kept verbatim in raw/<slug>.txt.

questions.title: Merge N-ary Trees by Node Key
questions.overview: Merge two N-ary trees whose nodes carry stable keys, combining nodes only when their keys match. The prompt is an N-ary transformation of the familiar binary-tree merge family, with conflict-policy and concurrent-update follow-ups.

questions.title: Weighted Sampling from a Probability Distribution
questions.overview: Given a probability distribution over `N` categories (e.g. an M-faced biased die or softmax weights), draw a sample in `O(log N)`. The canonical solution is inverse-CDF sampling — build a cumulative prefix and binary-search a uniform `[0, 1)` draw. Follow-ups dig into probabilities that don't sum to 1, very large or peaked distributions, and rejection-sampling expected cost.

questions.title: Phone Keypad — Letter Combinations / Word Filter
questions.overview: The classic phone-keypad letter-combinations problem shows up nearly every recent loop, often as the screen warm-up. A common variant: given a digit string and a dictionary of words, return which words can be typed on the keypad — the structural twist that turns it into a hash / trie problem rather than pure backtracking.

questions.title: Minimum Sum-of-Distances Meeting Point on a Line
questions.overview: Given a 1-D array of points, find the point that minimizes the sum of absolute distances to every other point. The answer is the median; the interview signal is the proof, not the code. Follow-ups extend to L2 distance with k chosen positions (much harder) and to streaming median maintenance.

questions.title: LRU Cache + Thread-Safe Follow-up
questions.overview: Implement an LRU cache, then extend to a thread-safe version. In post-reform loops this is often delivered as the AI-coding round: candidates outline the doubly-linked-list + hashmap design, let the in-IDE assistant produce the skeleton, then dry-run unit tests and reason about lock granularity.

questions.title: Recommender Training Pipeline
questions.overview: Complete a text-embedding recommender training pipeline using member profiles, item text, and clicked/skipped labels. Implement the RecommenderTrainer data-loading, feature-preparation, and training methods; the interviewer also requested a handwritten MLP.

questions.title: Nested List Weight Sum II (LC 364)
questions.overview: Compute the inverse-depth-weighted sum of integers in a nested list. The candidate explicitly identified this as unchanged LeetCode 364.

questions.title: Logistic Regression Debugging
questions.overview: Debug a logistic-regression implementation with errors in the weight gradient, sigmoid-derivative contract, and binary cross-entropy loss. The interviewer expects the corrected gradient to be derived and simplified to its final matrix form.

questions.title: Robot Navigation in an Unknown Grid
questions.overview: Control a robot in an initially unexplored matrix using turn, forward-move, wall-detection, and return-to-explored-location operations. Discover traversable cells while finding a path from the starting position to the destination.

questions.title: Count Distinct Values in a Massive Sorted Array
questions.overview: Count distinct values in a sorted array where `n` may be in the billions but the number of distinct values `k` is only in the hundreds. Skip each equal-value run with boundary searches for O(k log n), and analyze a divide-and-conquer alternative that can degrade to O(n).

questions.title: Find K Closest Elements in a Sorted Array (LC 658)
questions.overview: Given a sorted array, target `x`, and integer `k`, return the `k` closest values in sorted order, preferring the smaller value on equal distance. Implement the binary-search-on-window solution and discuss unsorted-input and out-of-memory variants.

questions.title: Pow(x, n) (LC 50)
questions.overview: Implement `pow(x, n)` for positive and negative integer exponents. The round expects an O(log n) solution in both recursive and iterative form, plus explicit handling of the minimum signed-integer exponent where ordinary negation overflows.

questions.title: 2-D Matrix Range Sum with Updates (OA SumTable)
questions.overview: HackerRank OA for the SWE AI Trainer (LLM rater) role. Five TypeScript multiple-choice questions on code-quality judgement plus one Python implementation: process a stream of `get`/`set` queries against a 2-D matrix returning the rectangle sum for `get` and applying point updates for `set`.

questions.title: Stratified Sampling from Class-Bucketed JSON
questions.overview: ML-coding sub-round (~20 min slot inside a triple-task phone screen). Input is a JSON object keyed by class label; the values are example arrays. Implement a uniform-over-classes sampler — pick a class uniformly at random first, then sample one example from that class.

questions.title: Cache with Rank-Based Eviction Policy
questions.overview: Given an interface where every cached value implements `rank()`, build a cache whose eviction policy drops the lowest-`rank()` entry on overflow. Hashmap plus a min-heap on `rank` is the baseline; the interesting follow-up is a stable last-seen-timestamp tiebreaker via doubly-linked-list bookkeeping per rank bucket.

questions.title: Service Dependency Impact Propagation
questions.overview: Given a JSON manifest mapping services to their `read_from` and `write_to` paths, and a list of deleted paths, identify which services are impacted. Three escalating sub-tasks layer a directory-tree projection and a service dependency chain on top of a basic intersection scan. The AI-coding round template — long prompt, IDE-context loading, assistant-driven implementation.

questions.title: Sparse Vector / Matrix Product
questions.overview: Design `SparseVector` and `SparseMatrix` classes from scratch, then implement vector-vector and matrix-matrix products without materializing the dense form. The bar is *both* sub-`O(M × N)` time and minimal memory — a list-of-coordinates representation is the expected baseline; CSR/CSC if pushed.

questions.title: Count Subarrays Where First = Last = Max
questions.overview: Count subarrays where the first element equals the last element equals the maximum value in the subarray. Not a canonical LC problem; the optimal `O(N)` solution uses a monotonic-decreasing stack to find, for each index, the next strictly greater element on the right and group equal-value runs accordingly.

questions.title: Ranked-Choice Voting (Instant Runoff)
questions.overview: Implement instant-runoff voting: each voter submits a preference ranking; in each round, the lowest-vote candidate is eliminated and that candidate's votes redistribute to their next-preferred remaining candidate. Return the candidate that first crosses 50%. Pure simulation with care needed on tie-breaking and ballot iteration pointers.

questions.title: Largest Number (LC 179)
questions.overview: Arrange non-negative integers to form the largest concatenated number. The standard formulation returns a string; any interview-specific modifications remain unspecified.

questions.title: LFU Cache
questions.overview: LeetCode 460 — implement an `O(1)` LFU cache. Two hashmaps (key→node, freq→doubly-linked-list) plus a `min_freq` cursor. Surfaces in both phone screens and onsite coding rounds, often as the candidate's second algorithmic problem in a tight window.

questions.title: Max Stack
questions.overview: LeetCode 716: implement a stack with `push`, `pop`, `top`, `peekMax`, and `popMax`. The `popMax` operation is the discriminator — the optimal answer is a doubly-linked list of nodes plus a TreeMap (or skip list) keyed on value, giving `O(log N)` for `popMax` and `O(1)` for the rest.

questions.title: Biased Coin to Uniform Range
questions.overview: Given a biased Bernoulli (returns 0 with probability `p`, 1 with probability `1-p`), construct a uniform sampler over `[0, 6]`. The canonical recipe: combine two biased draws to get a fair coin (Von Neumann's trick), then bit-pack three fair coins and reject draws outside `[0, 6]`.

questions.title: Meeting Scheduler — Earliest Available Slot
questions.overview: Given a list of existing meetings and a new meeting's required start-time-no-earlier-than and duration, return the earliest start that fits. Delivered as the AI-coding round in recent loops — the interviewer watches whether the candidate uses the assistant for boilerplate while keeping the data-structure decision (sorted-by-start with binary search vs segment tree) under their own control.

questions.title: Alert Monitor — Rolling Window + Severity Distribution + Spike Detection
questions.overview: Build an `AlertMonitor` class with three queries against an append-only stream: count alerts in the trailing 15 minutes, return the severity histogram for the current hour-block, and emit a next-greater-volume index per minute. The third sub-task is monotonic-stack territory; the round tests whether the candidate picks the right data structure for each query rather than retrofitting one structure for everything.

questions.title: Function Inclusive / Exclusive Time
questions.overview: Given a list of `(function_id, start|end, timestamp)` log lines, compute the inclusive and exclusive elapsed time for a target function. LeetCode 636 variant — stack-based bookkeeping where each `start` pushes a context and each `end` pops while attributing elapsed time to the *current top* of the stack.

questions.title: Distributed Job Scheduler / Calendar Service
questions.overview: Design a job scheduler / calendar service that supports millions of scheduled tasks, range queries for upcoming tasks, and real-time dashboard updates. Variants include event scheduling with timezones and recurring events.

questions.title: AI-Powered Personalized Recruiter Message Generation
questions.overview: Design an end-to-end system that helps recruiters generate personalised outreach: pull the candidate profile, the open role, the recruiter's past outreach style, and produce a draft InMail. Recurring sub-prompts cover tool registration, RAG, LLM fine-tuning vs prompting, draft / human-in-the-loop, and offline + online evaluation.

questions.title: Metrics & Monitoring Platform
questions.overview: Design a metrics platform that ingests production telemetry, supports arbitrary-granularity queries, and powers a visualization layer. Recurring twists: `top-k` exceptions by error class, severity histograms over time, and explicit *no-alerting* scope (the interviewer wants you to scope tight and not drift into pager design).

questions.title: News Feed / Timeline
questions.overview: Design a ranked news feed for a read-heavy social product with seconds-level freshness. Use a hybrid fan-out strategy, lightweight per-user inboxes, asynchronous celebrity delivery, bounded history, two-stage ranking, and explicit read-your-writes handling for a user's own posts.

questions.title: Real-Time Collaborative Code Editor
questions.overview: Design a CoderPad-like session: one admin can edit, all viewers see real-time updates, new joiners catch up immediately, optional code execution. The interviewer explicitly forbids referring to operational-transform algorithms — derive the propagation model from scratch.

questions.title: Type-Ahead / Autocomplete Suggestions
questions.overview: Design a type-ahead service that returns the top-K most relevant completions for a query prefix in `< 100 ms`. Recurring follow-ups: personalisation, multi-region freshness, and tail-latency budget when the trie spans hundreds of millions of phrases.

questions.title: LinkedIn Learning / Job Recommendation Ranking
questions.overview: Design a recommender that surfaces LinkedIn Learning courses (or jobs) based on the user's profile, recently applied jobs, and behavioural history. Standard candidate-generation + ranking architecture; the LinkedIn-specific twist is heavy feature engineering on the job-posting side and explicit explainability for the recommended item.

questions.title: LinkedIn Skills — Data Mining & ML System Design
questions.overview: Design the pipeline behind LinkedIn's Skills graph: how skill phrases are extracted from resumes / job posts, normalized into a canonical taxonomy, ranked per profile, and continually updated as new skills emerge. The round is graded as much on data collection / labeling strategy as on modeling.

questions.title: Single-Machine Key-Value Store with Filesystem Spill
questions.overview: Design a single-machine KV store that holds a billion keys and MB-scale values. Memory is bounded; on-disk format is append-only files; values cannot live entirely in memory. The round straddles system design and data-structure design — many candidates over-pivot to distributed systems and lose signal.

questions.title: Project Deep-Dive (Four-Axis Rubric)
questions.overview: Conversational deep-dive on one or two recent projects, graded against four axes: Leadership, Craftsmanship, Execution, Impact. Bring an architecture diagram (white-board or pre-drawn) and lead the interviewer through with two-to-three years of context. The round runs from `phone screen` through `onsite` depending on level.

questions.title: Behavioral / BQ Question Pack (Staff & Senior)
questions.overview: Recurring behavioral prompts across recent loops, especially at Staff level. LinkedIn's bar is explicit about *leadership narrative depth* — interviewers flag when a Staff candidate's stories sound like Senior-IC work. Bring two-to-three multi-quarter, cross-functional stories with quantified business impact for each top theme.
